units.2 Kings 18:17: The king of the Assyrians sent Tharthan, Raphis, and Rhapsakes from Lachish to King Hezekiah against Jerusalem with a great force. They went up, came to Jerusalem, and stood at the aqueduct of the upper pool, on the road of the Fuller’s Field.
units.2 Kings 18:18: They called to Hezekiah. Eliakim son of Chelkias the steward, Somnas the scribe, and Joash son of Asaph the recorder went out to him.
units.2 Kings 18:19: Rhapsakes said to them, ‘Tell Hezekiah: Thus says the great king, the king of the Assyrians: What is this confidence in which you trust?
units.2 Kings 18:20: You said—only words of lips!—“Counsel and strength for war.” Now then, in whom do you trust, that you have broken with me?
units.2 Kings 18:21: Now behold, you have put your trust in this broken reed staff, Egypt. If a man supports himself on it, it enters his hand and pierces it. So is Pharaoh king of Egypt to all who trust him.
units.2 Kings 18:22: Since you said to me, “We trust the Lord God,” is He not the One whose high places and altars Hezekiah removed, saying to Judah and Jerusalem, “Before this altar you shall bow down in Jerusalem”?
units.2 Kings 18:23: Now join yourselves to my master, the king of the Assyrians. I will give you two thousand horses if you can provide riders for them.
units.2 Kings 18:24: How can you turn back the face of one district governor, one of my master’s least servants? Yet you hope in Egypt for chariots and horsemen!
units.2 Kings 18:25: Now have we come up without the Lord against this place to destroy it? The Lord said to me, “Go up against this land and destroy it.”’
units.2 Kings 18:26: Eliakim son of Chelkias, Somnas, and Joash said to Rhapsakes, ‘Please speak to your servants in Syrian, for we understand it. Do not speak with us in Judean. Why are you speaking within the hearing of the people on the wall?’
units.2 Kings 18:27: Rhapsakes said to them, ‘Has my master sent me to speak these words to your master and to you? Was it not to the men sitting on the wall, who are to eat their own dung and drink their own urine together with you?’
units.2 Kings 18:28: Rhapsakes stood and cried out loudly in Judean: ‘Hear the words of the great king of the Assyrians!
units.2 Kings 18:29: Thus says the king: Do not let Hezekiah lift you up with words, for he cannot rescue you from my hand.
units.2 Kings 18:30: Do not let Hezekiah make you hope in the Lord by saying, “The Lord will surely rescue us; this city will certainly not be handed into the hand of the king of the Assyrians.”
units.2 Kings 18:31: Do not listen to Hezekiah, for thus says the king of the Assyrians: Make a blessing with me and come out to me. Each man shall drink from his vine, eat from his fig tree, and drink water from his cistern,
units.2 Kings 18:32: until I come and take you to a land like your own, a land of grain, wine, bread, and vineyards, a land of oil-bearing olives and honey. You will live and certainly not die. Do not listen to Hezekiah, because he deceives you, saying, “The Lord will rescue us.”
units.2 Kings 18:33: Have the gods of the nations ever rescued, each his own country, from the hand of the king of the Assyrians?
units.2 Kings 18:34: Where is the god of Aimath and Arphad? Where is the god of Seppharouain? And have they rescued Samaria from my hand?
units.2 Kings 18:35: Who among all the gods of the lands has rescued their lands from my hand, that the Lord should rescue Jerusalem from my hand?’
units.2 Kings 18:36: They kept silent and did not answer him a word, for the king had commanded, ‘Do not answer him.’
units.2 Kings 18:37: Eliakim son of Chelkias the steward, Somnas the scribe, and Joash son of Asaph the recorder came to Hezekiah with torn garments and reported Rhapsakes’s words to him.
units.Isaiah 7:1: In the days of Achaz, son of Joatham, son of Oziah, king of Judea, Raasson king of Aram and Phakee son of Romelias, king of Israel, went up against Jerusalem to wage war on her, but they could not besiege her.
units.Isaiah 7:2: It was reported to David’s house, “Aram has come to agreement with Ephraim.” His soul and his people’s soul were distraught, as when a tree in a wood is shaken by wind.
units.Isaiah 7:3: The Lord said to Isaiah, “Go out to meet Achaz, you and the remaining Jasub, your son, toward the pool of the upper road of the fuller’s field,
units.Isaiah 7:4: and you will say to him, ‘Take care to be quiet, and do not fear; do not let your soul grow weak before these two smoking firebrand logs. For whenever the wrath of My anger comes, I will heal again.
units.2 Samuel 23:1: These are David’s last words: “Faithful is David son of Jesse, and faithful the man whom the Lord raised up as the anointed of the God of Jacob; beautiful are Israel’s psalms.
units.2 Samuel 23:2: The Spirit of the Lord spoke in me; His word was upon my tongue.
units.2 Samuel 23:3: The God of Israel says; the Guard of Israel spoke to me: ‘Speak a parable: How will you all strengthen the fear of God in a human being?
units.2 Samuel 23:4: May the sun rise in God’s morning light; the morning did not pass away from brightness, and like grass from rain out of the earth.’
units.2 Samuel 23:5: For is not my house so with the Mighty One? He established an everlasting covenant with me, ready at every time, guarded; for all my salvation and every desire—surely the lawless one will not sprout.
units.Micah 4:1: In the last days the mountain of the Lord will be manifest, established upon the mountain summits and raised above the hills, and peoples will hurry toward it.
units.Micah 4:2: Many nations will go and say, “Come, let us go up to the Lord’s mountain and to the house of Jacob’s God. They will show us His way, and we will walk in His paths.” For law will go out from Zion, and the Lord’s word from Jerusalem.
units.Micah 4:3: He will judge between many peoples and reprove strong nations as far as a distant land. They will cut their swords into plows and their spears into sickles. Nation will certainly no longer raise sword against nation, nor will they learn to wage war anymore.
units.Micah 4:4: Each will rest beneath his vine and each beneath his fig tree, and there will be no one causing fear, because the mouth of the Lord Almighty has spoken these things.
units.Micah 4:5: For all the peoples will walk, each his own way, but we will walk in the name of the Lord our God forever and beyond.
units.Psalms 17:1: For the end. Of the Lord’s servant David, who spoke the words of this song to the Lord on the day the Lord rescued him from the hand of all his enemies and from the hand of Saul.
units.Psalms 17:2: And he said: I will love Thee, Lord, my strength.
units.Psalms 17:3: The Lord is my firm foundation, my refuge, and my rescuer; my God is my helper, and I will hope in Him; my protector, the horn of my salvation, my supporter.
units.Psalms 17:4: Praising, I will call upon the Lord, and I will be saved from my enemies.
units.Psalms 17:5: The birth pangs of death encompassed me, and torrents of lawlessness threw me into turmoil.
units.Psalms 17:6: The birth pangs of Hades surrounded me; the traps of death overtook me.
units.Psalms 17:7: And when I was afflicted, I called upon the Lord and cried out to my God. He heard my voice from His holy temple, and my cry before Him will enter His ears.
units.Job 20:2: “I did not expect you to answer back like this, and you all do not understand more than I do.
units.Job 20:3: I will hear correction that puts me to shame, and a spirit from understanding answers me.
units.Matthew 23:1: Then Jesus spoke to the crowds and His disciples,
units.Matthew 23:2: saying, “The scribes and Pharisees have seated themselves in Moses’ chair.
units.Matthew 23:3: Therefore do and observe everything they tell you, but do not act according to their works, for they say and do not do.
units.Luke 19:28: And after saying these things, He went on ahead, going up to Jerusalem.
units.Luke 19:29: And it happened that as He drew near Bethphage and Bethany, at the mount called Olivet, He sent two of the disciples,
units.Luke 19:30: saying, “Go into the village opposite. As you enter it, you will find a colt tied, on which no person has ever sat. Untie it and bring it.
units.Luke 19:31: And if anyone asks you, ‘Why are you untying it?’ you shall say this: ‘The Lord has need of it.’”
units.Luke 19:32: Those who were sent went away and found it just as He had told them.
units.Luke 19:33: As they were untying the colt, its owners said to them, “Why are you untying the colt?”
units.Luke 19:34: And they said, “The Lord has need of it.”
units.Luke 19:35: They brought it to Jesus, threw their garments on the colt, and set Jesus upon it.
units.Luke 19:36: As He went, they spread their own garments on the road.
units.Luke 19:37: As He was already drawing near the descent of the Mount of Olives, the whole multitude of the disciples began to rejoice and praise God with a loud voice for all the mighty works they had seen,
units.Luke 19:38: saying, “Blessed is the King who comes in the name of the Lord! Peace in heaven, and glory in the highest!”
units.Luke 19:39: And some of the Pharisees from the crowd said to Him, “Teacher, rebuke Thy disciples.”
units.Luke 19:40: And He answered, “I tell you, if these fall silent, the stones will cry out.”
units.Acts 1:1: In my first account, Theophilus, I wrote about all that Jesus began both to do and to teach
units.Acts 1:2: until the day when, after giving instructions through the Holy Spirit to the apostles whom He had chosen, He was taken up.
units.Acts 1:3: To them He also presented Himself alive after His suffering, with many proofs, appearing to them over forty days and speaking about the kingdom of God.
units.Acts 1:4: While gathered with them, He ordered them not to leave Jerusalem, but to wait for the Father’s promise, “which,” He said, “you heard from Me;
units.Acts 1:5: for John baptized with water, but you will be baptized in the Holy Spirit not many days from now.”
units.Mark 13:1: As He was leaving the temple, one of His disciples said to Him, “Teacher, look! What stones and what buildings!”
units.Mark 13:2: Jesus said to him, “Do you see these great buildings? Not one stone will be left here on another that will not be torn down.”
units.Mark 13:3: As He sat on the Mount of Olives opposite the temple, Peter, James, John, and Andrew questioned Him privately:
units.Mark 13:4: “Tell us, when will these things be, and what will be the sign when all these things are about to be fulfilled?”
units.Mark 13:5: Jesus began saying to them, “Watch out that no one leads you astray.
units.Mark 13:6: Many will come in My name, saying, ‘I am he,’ and will lead many astray.
units.Mark 13:7: When you hear of wars and reports of wars, do not be alarmed. These must happen, but the end is not yet.
units.Mark 13:8: For nation will rise against nation, and kingdom against kingdom. There will be earthquakes in various places; there will be famines. These things are the beginning of birth pains.
units.Isaiah 28:1: Woe to the crown of insolence, Ephraim’s hired men; the flower fallen from glory on the summit of the fertile mountain, those drunk without wine!
units.Isaiah 28:2: Behold, the Lord’s wrath is strong and harsh, like falling hail with no covering, falling violently. Like a great mass of water dragging a country, He will give the land rest with His hands.
units.Isaiah 28:3: Underfoot will be trampled the crown of insolence, Ephraim’s hired men.
units.Isaiah 28:4: The flower fallen from the hope of glory, on the high mountain’s summit, will be like an early fig: whoever sees it will want to swallow it before taking it into his hand.
units.Isaiah 28:5: On that day the Lord Sabaoth will be the crown of hope, woven of glory, for My people who remain;
units.Isaiah 28:6: they will be left with a spirit of judgment, for judgment and strength, as He prevents destruction.
units.Isaiah 28:7: For these have been led astray by wine and wandered because of sikera. Priest and prophet lost their senses because of wine, reeled from sikera’s intoxication and went astray. This is an apparition.
units.Isaiah 28:8: A curse will consume this counsel, for this counsel is for greed.
units.Isaiah 28:9: To whom did we announce evils, and to whom did we announce a message—you weaned from milk, torn from a breast?
units.Isaiah 28:10: Expect affliction upon affliction, hope upon hope, yet a little, yet a little,
units.Isaiah 28:11: because of contemptuous lips, through another tongue, for they will speak to this people,
units.Isaiah 28:12: saying to it, “This is the rest for the hungry, and this is the shattering.” But they did not want to listen.
units.Isaiah 28:13: The utterance of the Lord God will become for them affliction upon affliction, hope upon hope, yet a little, yet a little, so that they go and fall backward, come into danger, be shattered and captured.
units.Isaiah 28:14: Therefore hear the Lord’s word, afflicted men and rulers of this people in Jerusalem:
units.Isaiah 28:15: Because you said, “We made a covenant with Hades and agreements with death; if a rushing storm passes, it will certainly not come upon us. We made falsehood our hope and will be sheltered by deceit,”
units.Isaiah 28:16: therefore thus says the Lord: “Behold, I will place in Zion’s foundations a costly, chosen, precious cornerstone, in her foundations, and whoever trusts in it will certainly not be ashamed.
units.Isaiah 28:17: I will make judgment a hope, and My mercy will be weights; those trusting deceit do so in vain, for a storm will certainly not pass you by—
units.Isaiah 28:18: might it also remove your covenant with death? Your hope toward Hades will certainly not remain. If a rushing storm comes, you will become its trampling ground.
units.Isaiah 28:19: When it passes, it will take you; morning after morning it will pass during the day, and at night there will be evil hope. Learn to listen!
units.Isaiah 28:20: Cramped, we cannot fight, and we ourselves are too weak to be gathered.
units.Isaiah 28:21: Like a mountain of ungodly people he will rise and be in Gabaon’s ravine. With wrath he will do his deeds, a work of bitterness; his wrath will act strangely, and his bitterness is foreign.”
units.Isaiah 28:22: And you, do not rejoice, nor let your bonds grow stronger, because I heard from the Lord Sabaoth completed and shortened deeds, which He will do upon all the earth.
units.Isaiah 28:23: Give ear and hear my voice; pay attention and hear my words.
units.Isaiah 28:24: Will the plowman plow all day? Or will he prepare seed before working the ground?
units.Isaiah 28:25: When he has leveled its surface, does he not then sow a little black cumin and cumin, and again sow wheat, barley and emmer within your borders?
units.Isaiah 28:26: You will be disciplined by your God’s judgment and will rejoice.
units.Isaiah 28:27: For black cumin is not cleaned with harshness, nor will a wagon wheel roll over cumin; black cumin is shaken out with a rod, but cumin
units.Isaiah 28:28: will be eaten with bread. For I will not be angry with you for ever, nor will the sound of My bitterness trample you.
units.Isaiah 28:29: These wonders too came from the Lord Sabaoth. Take counsel; raise up futile consolation!
units.Isaiah 29:1: Woe, city Ariel, against which David fought! Gather produce year after year, for you will eat with Moab.
units.Isaiah 29:2: For I will press Ariel hard, and her strength and wealth will be Mine.
units.Isaiah 29:3: I will surround you like David, set a palisade around you and set towers around you,
units.Isaiah 29:4: and your words will be humbled into the earth and sink into the earth. Your voice will be like those who speak from the earth, and your voice will weaken toward the ground.
units.Isaiah 29:5: The wealth of the ungodly will be like dust from a wheel, like drifting chaff, and it will be like a moment, immediately,
units.Isaiah 29:6: from the Lord Sabaoth. For there will be a visitation with thunder, earthquake and a great sound, a rushing storm and a consuming flame of fire.
units.Isaiah 29:7: Like someone dreaming in sleep will be the wealth of all nations who marched against Ariel, all who marched against Jerusalem, and all assembled against her and afflicting her.
units.Isaiah 29:8: They will be like people drinking and eating in sleep; when they rise, their dream is futile. As a thirsty person dreams of drinking but wakes still thirsty, his soul having hoped in vain, so will be the wealth of all nations who marched against Mount Zion.
units.Isaiah 29:9: Grow faint, lose your senses and suffer a hangover, neither from sikera nor from wine,
units.Isaiah 29:10: because the Lord has made you drink a spirit of stupor, and He will close their eyes and those of their prophets and rulers, those who see hidden things.
units.Isaiah 29:11: All these sayings will be for you like the words of this sealed book. If they give it to a person who knows how to read, saying, “Read these,” he will say, “I cannot read, for it is sealed.”
units.Isaiah 29:12: This book will be given into the hands of a person who does not know how to read. Someone will say to him, “Read this,” and he will say, “I do not know how to read.”
units.Isaiah 29:13: The Lord said, “This people draws near Me; with their lips they honor Me, but their heart is far from Me. They revere Me in vain, teaching human commands and teachings.
units.Isaiah 29:14: Therefore, behold, I will proceed to remove this people; I will remove them, destroy the wise people’s wisdom and hide the discerning people’s understanding.”
units.Isaiah 29:15: Woe to those making deep counsel, but not through the Lord! Woe to those making counsel in secret! Their deeds will be in darkness, and they will say, “Who has seen us, and who will know us or what we do?”
units.Isaiah 29:16: Will you not be reckoned as the potter’s clay? Will the formed thing say to its former, “You did not form me,” or the work to its maker, “You did not make me intelligently”?
units.Isaiah 29:17: Is it not yet a little while until Lebanon is changed like Mount Chermel, and Mount Chermel is reckoned as forest?
units.Isaiah 29:18: On that day the deaf will hear a book’s words, and the blind people’s eyes in darkness and mist will see.
units.Isaiah 29:19: The poor will exult with joy because of the Lord, and the hopeless among people will be filled with gladness.
units.Isaiah 29:20: The lawless one has failed, the arrogant one has perished, and those acting lawlessly for evil have been destroyed,
units.Isaiah 29:21: and those who cause people to sin by a word. They will make all who reprove at the gates a stumbling block, and have turned the righteous aside through injustices.
units.Isaiah 29:22: Therefore thus says the Lord concerning Jacob’s house, which He set apart from Abraham: “Jacob will not now be ashamed, nor will Israel now change his face;
units.Isaiah 29:23: but when their children see My works, because of Me they will sanctify My name, sanctify Jacob’s Holy One and fear Israel’s God.
units.Isaiah 29:24: Those wandering in spirit will know understanding; grumblers will learn obedience, and stammering tongues will learn to speak peace.”
units.Isaiah 30:1: “Woe, rebellious children,” thus says the Lord, “you made a plan not through Me and agreements not through My spirit, to add sins upon sins,
units.Isaiah 30:2: you who go down to Egypt, but they did not ask Me, to be helped by Pharaoh and sheltered by Egyptians.
units.Isaiah 30:3: For Pharaoh’s shelter will become your shame, and reproach for those trusting in Egypt.
units.Isaiah 30:4: For there are leaders in Tanis, evil messengers; they will labor in vain
units.Isaiah 30:5: toward a people that will not benefit them, neither for assistance nor for profit, but for shame and reproach.”
units.Isaiah 30:6: The vision of the four-footed creatures in the wilderness. In affliction and hardship, a lion and lion cub from there, asps and offspring of flying asps; they carried their wealth on donkeys and camels to a nation that will not benefit them with help, but with shame and reproach.
units.Isaiah 30:7: Egyptians will benefit you with futile and empty things. Announce to them, “This consolation of yours is futile.”
units.Isaiah 30:8: Now then, sit and write these things on a tablet and in a book, because these things will endure for days of appointed times and for ever.
units.Isaiah 30:9: For this is a disobedient people, lying sons who did not want to hear God’s law,
units.Isaiah 30:10: who say to the prophets, “Do not announce to us,” and to those seeing visions, “Do not speak to us. Instead, speak to us and announce another deception,
units.Isaiah 30:11: and turn us from this way, remove this path from us, and remove Israel’s Holy One from us.”
units.Isaiah 30:12: Therefore thus says the Lord, Israel’s Holy One: “Because you disobeyed these words and hoped in falsehood, and because you grumbled and came to trust in this word,
units.Isaiah 30:13: therefore this sin will be for you like a wall falling immediately in a captured fortified city, whose fall is immediately at hand,
units.Isaiah 30:14: and its fall will be like the shattering of an earthen vessel, fine pieces from a jar, so that no shard is found among them with which to lift fire or draw a little water.”
units.Isaiah 30:15: Thus says the Lord, Israel’s Holy One: “When you turn back and groan, then you will be saved and know where you were. When you trusted in futile things, your strength became futile.” But you did not want to listen,
units.Isaiah 30:16: but you said, “We will flee on horses.” Therefore you will flee. You said, “We will ride swift mounts.” Therefore those pursuing you will be swift.
units.Isaiah 30:17: At the voice of one, a thousand will flee; at the voice of five, many will flee, until you are left like a mast upon a mountain, like someone carrying a standard upon a hill.
units.Isaiah 30:18: Again God will wait to pity you, and therefore He will be exalted to have mercy on you, because the Lord our God is a judge. Where will you leave your glory? Blessed are those remaining in Him.
units.Isaiah 30:19: For a holy people will dwell in Zion, and Jerusalem wept bitterly, “Have mercy on me!” He will have mercy on you at the sound of your cry; when He saw, He listened to you.
units.Isaiah 30:20: The Lord will give you bread of affliction and scant water; those misleading you will certainly no longer approach you, for your eyes will see those misleading you,
units.Isaiah 30:21: and your ears will hear the words of those behind you who led you astray, saying, “This is the way; let us walk in it, whether right or left.”
units.Isaiah 30:22: You will remove the silver-covered and gold-covered idols, reduce them to fine pieces and winnow them like a menstruating woman’s fluid; like dung you will push them away.
units.Isaiah 30:23: Then there will be rain for your land’s seed; bread from your land’s produce will be plentiful and rich, and on that day your livestock will graze a fertile, spacious place,
units.Isaiah 30:24: your bulls and cattle working the earth will eat straw prepared with barley and winnowed.
units.Isaiah 30:25: On every high mountain and every lofty hill there will be flowing water on that day, when many perish and towers fall.
units.Isaiah 30:26: The moon’s light will be like the sun’s light, and the sun’s light will be sevenfold on the day when the Lord heals His people’s fracture; He will heal the pain of your wound.
units.Isaiah 30:27: Behold, the Lord’s name comes after a long time, wrath burning. His lips’ utterance comes with glory, an utterance full of anger, and the anger of His wrath will consume like fire.
units.Isaiah 30:28: His spirit will come like water sweeping through a ravine, reaching the neck, and will divide to trouble nations in futile wandering. Delusion will pursue them and seize them in their faces.
units.Isaiah 30:29: Must you always rejoice and always enter My holy places like festival-keepers, like people rejoicing as they enter with a flute to the Lord’s mountain, to Israel’s God?
units.Isaiah 30:30: God will make His voice’s glory heard and show His arm’s wrath with fury, anger and consuming flame. He will strike violently with lightning, like water and hail falling together violently.
units.Isaiah 30:31: For at the Lord’s voice the Assyrians will be defeated by the blow with which He strikes them.
units.Isaiah 30:32: It will be all around him, from where he hoped for help, on which he himself relied; they will turn and fight him with flutes and a lyre.
units.Isaiah 30:33: For you will be called to account ahead of time. Has it also been prepared for you to rule a deep ravine, with wood laid out, fire and much wood? The Lord’s wrath is like a ravine burning with sulfur.
units.Isaiah 31:1: Woe to those going down to Egypt for help, trusting in horses and chariots because there are many, and in horses, a very great multitude, but not trusting Israel’s Holy One or seeking God!
units.Isaiah 31:2: He Himself, wise, brought evils upon them; His word will certainly not be set aside. He will rise against evil people’s houses and against their futile hope,
units.Isaiah 31:3: an Egyptian human being and not God, horses’ flesh, with no help. The Lord will bring His hand against them; the helpers will grow weary, and all will perish together.
units.Isaiah 31:4: For thus the Lord said to me: “As a lion or lion cub cries over prey it has caught and shouts over it until the mountains fill with its voice, and they are defeated and terrified by the greatness of its wrath, so the Lord Sabaoth will descend to march upon Mount Zion, upon her mountains.
units.Isaiah 31:5: Like flying birds, so the Lord will shield Jerusalem, rescue, preserve and save.”
units.Isaiah 31:6: Turn back, you planning a deep and lawless plan.
units.Isaiah 31:7: For on that day people will renounce their silver and golden handmade things, which their hands made.
units.Isaiah 31:8: Assour will fall. Neither a man’s sword nor a human’s sword will devour him, and he will flee, but not from a sword. The young men will be defeated,
units.Isaiah 31:9: for they will be enclosed by a rock as by a palisade and defeated, and the fugitive will be captured. Thus says the Lord: “Blessed is the one who has seed in Zion and household members in Jerusalem.”
units.Isaiah 32:1: For behold, a righteous king will reign, and rulers will rule with judgment.
units.Isaiah 32:2: The man will conceal his words and hide as from rushing water; he will appear in Zion like a rushing river, glorious in a thirsty land.
units.Isaiah 32:3: They will no longer trust in human beings, but will give their ears to listen.
units.Isaiah 32:4: The heart of the weak will pay attention and listen, and stammering tongues will quickly learn to speak peace.
units.Isaiah 32:5: They will no longer tell the fool to rule, and your attendants will no longer say, “Be silent.”
units.Isaiah 32:6: For the fool will speak foolish things, and his heart will think futile things, carrying out lawless acts and speaking deception toward the Lord, scattering hungry souls and making thirsty souls empty.
units.Isaiah 32:7: For evil people’s counsel will devise lawless things, to destroy the lowly with unjust words and scatter the lowly people’s words in judgment.
units.Isaiah 32:8: The devout made wise plans, and this counsel will remain.
units.Isaiah 32:9: Wealthy women, rise and hear my voice! Daughters in hope, hear my words!
units.Isaiah 32:10: Remember the days of a year in pain with hope; the vintage has been exhausted, the sowing has ceased and will certainly no longer come.
units.Isaiah 32:11: Be dismayed, grieve, you confident women; undress, become naked and wrap sackcloth around your waists,
units.Isaiah 32:12: and beat your breasts because of the desirable field and fruitful vine.
units.Isaiah 32:13: My people’s earth will grow thorn and grass, and joy will be removed from every house. Wealthy city,
units.Isaiah 32:14: houses abandoned! They will leave the city’s wealth and desirable houses; villages will become caves for ever, wild donkeys’ delight, pastures for shepherds,
units.Isaiah 32:15: until a spirit from on high comes upon you. Chermel will become wilderness, and Chermel will be reckoned as forest.
units.Isaiah 32:16: Judgment will rest in the wilderness, and righteousness will dwell in Carmel.
units.Isaiah 32:17: The works of righteousness will be peace; righteousness will secure rest, and they will be confident for ever.
units.Isaiah 32:18: His people will dwell in a city of peace and live confidently, and they will rest with wealth.
units.Isaiah 32:19: If hail comes down, it will not come upon you. Those dwelling in the forests will be confident like those in the plain.
units.Isaiah 32:20: Blessed are those sowing beside every water, where ox and donkey tread!
units.Isaiah 33:1: Woe to those afflicting you—yet no one afflicts you—and the one rejecting you does not reject. The rejecters will be captured and handed over; like a moth upon a cloak, so they will be defeated.
units.Isaiah 33:2: Lord, have mercy on us, for we have trusted in Thee. The disobedient people’s seed came to destruction, but our salvation is in a time of affliction.
units.Isaiah 33:3: At the sound of Thy terror, peoples were dismayed by fear of Thee, and nations scattered.
units.Isaiah 33:4: Now your spoils, small and great, will be gathered; as someone gathers locusts, so they will mock you.
units.Isaiah 33:5: Holy is God, who dwells on high; Zion has been filled with judgment and righteousness.
units.Isaiah 33:6: They will be handed over under law; our salvation is among treasures. There are wisdom, knowledge and reverence toward the Lord; these are treasures of righteousness.

units.Isaiah 36:1: In the fourteenth year of Hezekiah’s reign, Sennacherib king of the Assyrians came up against Judea’s fortified cities and took them.
units.Isaiah 36:2: The king of the Assyrians sent Rapsakes from Lachis to Jerusalem, to King Hezekiah, with a large force. He stood at the upper pool’s aqueduct, on the road of the fuller’s field.

units.Isaiah 36:7: But if you say, “We trust the Lord our God,”

units.Isaiah 36:10: Now have we come up without the Lord against this country to wage war upon it?’”

units.Isaiah 36:17: until I come and take you to a land like your land, a land of grain, wine, bread and vineyards.
units.Isaiah 36:18: Do not let Hezekiah deceive you, saying, “Your God will rescue you.” Have the nations’ gods each rescued his own country from the king of the Assyrians’ hand?

units.Isaiah 36:20: Which of all these nations’ gods rescued his land from my hand, that God should rescue Jerusalem from my hand?’”
